hook-1.text: This text is made of glass.

hook-2.text: Everything you see through it is live video, rendered frame by frame.

hook-3.text: Here's what it can do, how it works, and how to ship it at scale.

show-1.text: Chunky, frosted type, with real depth.

show-2.text: A lens that tracks the performer.

show-3.text: Reeded glass, slicing the scene into ribbons.

show-4.text: Frosted panels that react to the music.

show-5.text: Even water, rippling on the beat.

how-1.text: So how does it work? Three layers.

how-2.text: At the bottom, an E-F video element. Or any HTML at all.

how-3.text: In the middle, E-F surface mirrors those pixels onto a canvas, every single frame.

how-4.text: On top, a WebGL shader samples that canvas, and bends each pixel along the glass's surface normal.

how-5.text: Red, green and blue bend by slightly different amounts. That's the rainbow edge.

how-6.text: One frame task drives it all, on Editframe's clock. So every frame is deterministic.

how-7.text: So the same HTML renders in your browser, from the CLI, or in parallel on the Editframe API.

outro.text: Glass, at scale. Build it with Editframe.

show-6.text: Rain on a window. Every drop, a tiny lens.

show-7.text: And glass that shatters, straight into the next shot.
